  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Missing values: MCAR, MAR, and MNAR}

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(datagenerator)
```

`add_missingness()` takes a synthetic dataset and sets some values to `NA`.
The **mechanism** decides what the missingness depends on. This matters
because it decides whether ordinary analyses are biased.

```{r base}
base <- gen_correlated(
  n = 2000,
  means = c(income = 50, age = 45),
  sds = c(10, 12),
  cor = matrix(c(1, 0.5, 0.5, 1), 2),
  seed = 1
)
```

## MCAR: missing completely at random

Every value has the same chance of being missing, unrelated to any variable.

```{r mcar}
m1 <- add_missingness(base, prop = 0.2, mechanism = "MCAR", cols = "income", seed = 2)
c(mean_observed = mean(m1$income, na.rm = TRUE),
  mean_original = mean(base$income))
```

**Interpretation.** About 20% are missing, and the observed mean stays close to
the original. Dropping incomplete rows is unbiased here, only less precise.

## MAR: missing at random

The chance of missingness depends on an **observed** variable, here `age`.
Higher `age` means more missing `income`.

```{r mar}
m2 <- add_missingness(base, prop = 0.2, mechanism = "MAR", driver = "age",
                      cols = "income", strength = 2, seed = 2)
c(mean_age_when_income_missing = mean(m2$age[is.na(m2$income)]),
  mean_age_when_income_observed = mean(m2$age[!is.na(m2$income)]))
```

**Interpretation.** Rows with missing income are older on average. Dropping
them biases the mean income. Methods that condition on `age` (such as
multiple imputation) can correct this when `age` is recorded.

## MNAR: missing not at random

The chance of missingness depends on the **missing value itself**. Here, higher
incomes are more likely to be hidden.

```{r mnar}
m3 <- add_missingness(base, prop = 0.2, mechanism = "MNAR", cols = "income",
                      strength = 2, seed = 2)
c(mean_income_when_missing = mean(base$income[is.na(m3$income)]),
  mean_income_when_observed = mean(base$income[!is.na(m3$income)]))
```

**Interpretation.** The missing incomes were higher on average. The observed
data cannot show this, so the result depends on an assumption you cannot
check from the data. Use MNAR to test how sensitive your conclusions are.

## Provenance

Every call records its mechanism and its achieved rate in the provenance
record:

```{r meta}
dg_meta(m2)$missingness[c("mechanism", "prop", "strength", "driver", "achieved_rate")]
```
